tool.name: Spectrophotometer, EDXRF and LA-ICP-MS
tool.measures: the trace elements of the stone, which betray its deposit of origin
tips: A stone has only one origin, but several instruments confirm it
Compare ratios of elements, not a single element
LA-ICP-MS leaves a microscopic mark on the stone

steps.title: Why origin matters
steps.text: A ruby from Burma is not worth a ruby from Thailand, even if they look alike. Geographic origin changes the price, sometimes by a factor of ten. It cannot be read by eye: it is the laboratory that determines it.

steps.title: Trace elements
steps.text: Each deposit has its own “recipe” of small chemical elements: iron, chromium, vanadium, titanium, gallium, copper... They are present in tiny amounts (a few millionths), but their proportions vary from one deposit to another. This is the fingerprint that is measured.

steps.title: The three instruments
steps.text: • The UV-Vis-NIR spectrophotometer measures the absorption of light from the ultraviolet to the near infrared: the spectra reveal iron, chromium, vanadium, titanium. • EDXRF excites the stone with X-rays: each element answers with its lines, the more intense the more abundant it is. Fast, and it leaves no trace. • LA-ICP-MS vaporizes a microscopic amount of material with a laser and passes it into the mass spectrometer: the reference measurement, the most precise.

steps.title: Confirming the origin
steps.text: You never rely on a single instrument. The results are compared with the known values of each deposit: if several measurements agree, the origin is confirmed. If they contradict each other, the stone stays “origin undetermined”. A treated stone (by beryllium diffusion, for example) can blur the measurement: you have to know it.

steps.title: To remember
steps.text: • Origin is read in the trace elements. • Spectrophotometer (light), EDXRF (X-rays), LA-ICP-MS (laser and mass): from the simplest to the most precise. • A rare and renowned origin greatly increases the value of the stone.
